source.title: Imbalance in habitual versus goal directed neural systems during symptom provocation in obsessive-compulsive disorder.

confidence_rationale: Symptom-provocation fMRI that separately models the urge-to-avoid, rejection, and RELIEF events of a compulsive cycle, finding goal-directed (caudate-prefrontal) deactivation alongside habitual (putamen/STN) hyperactivation, with putaminal activity preceding the avoidance-and-relief sequence. Supports Q-063 on two fronts: an imbalance toward habitual control during compulsion (the stickiness limb) AND a neural correlate of the release/relief event -- the analogue of Q-063's SD-034 closure-operator 'fires and releases' diagnostic. Held at 0.6 because it is correlational neuroimaging that does not separate value from stickiness directly, and the relief-event mapping to a closure operator is a structural analogy.
failure_signatures: Strong symptom provocation evoked caudate-prefrontal DEACTIVATION with putaminal/STN hyperactivation -- a loop that proceeds while the goal-directed (value) circuit is offline; a value-only readout would see this trapped loop as having no active goal representation, mistaking absent z_goal for low value.

The relief event followed putaminal hyperactivation then deactivation -- if REE's closure operator never fires (no relief transition) the loop is blocked by decommit-friction, not released by value; absence of a relief/release signature is the tell for a trapped loop.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During individually-tailored symptom provocation, OCD patients showed a dichotomous deactivation of caudate-prefrontal (goal-directed) circuits with hyperactivation of subthalamic-nucleus/putaminal (habit) regions; putaminal hyperactivation during provocation preceded subsequent deactivation during the avoidance and RELIEF events, with ventromedial-prefrontal/orbitofrontal cortex modulating the compulsivity circuit.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports Q-063's stickiness limb (compulsion runs with goal-directed/value circuitry deactivated) and, more specifically, supplies a neural analogue of the SD-034 closure-operator 'fires-and-releases' diagnostic: the provocation -> urge -> avoidance -> relief sequence is the biological cousin of REE's commit -> dwell -> release trajectory, and a trapped loop is one where the release/relief transition fails to fire.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Correlational fMRI during symptom provocation, not a manipulation that separates value from stickiness; 'relief' is the subjective/neural cessation of an aversive urge, which maps to REE's closure-operator release only by structural analogy, not by measuring the same variable. Small sample (15 patients).
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI: 15 OCD patients + 15 controls, individualised live symptom-provocation paradigm with trial-by-trial avoidance responses and modelled relief events.

confidence_components.notes: Brain journal, novel ecological design, but small sample and correlational; mapping to the closure-operator release event is a structural analogy, lowering mapping_fidelity.
